Coplanarity condition: Three vectors are coplanar (lie in the same plane) if and only if their scalar triple product is zero: a · (b × c) = 0.
Non-coplanar vectors: If the scalar triple product is non-zero, the three vectors are linearly independent and form a basis for 3D space.
The vector triple product is defined as:
Mnemonic (BAC-CAB): Remember as 'BAC minus CAB' — the order of vectors in the dot products is B then A then C, minus C then A then B.
Scalar triple product of parallel vectors: If any two of a, b, c are parallel, the scalar triple product is 0.
Vector triple product of collinear vectors: If b and c are parallel, then b × c = 0, so a × (b × c) = 0.
Volume of tetrahedron: If OABC is a tetrahedron with position vectors a, b, c for A, B, C respectively, then V = (1/6)|a · (b × c)|.
Checking coplanarity: Three points with position vectors a, b, c and a fourth point d are coplanar if (b − a) · ((c − a) × (d − a)) = 0.
Resolution of vectors: The vector triple product formula is used to resolve a vector into components parallel and perpendicular to a given direction.
Distance from point to plane: If n is a normal to the plane and a is a point on the plane, the distance from point b to the plane is |(b−a)·n|/|n|.
Volume of pyramid: For a pyramid with triangular base formed by a, b, c and apex at origin, volume = (1/6)|a · (b × c)|.
confusion: The BAC-CAB rule: a × (b × c) = (a · c)b − (a · b)c. Do NOT reverse the terms — it is BAC minus CAB, not ABC minus ACB.
The vector triple product a × (b × c) is NOT equal to (a × b) × c. The cross product is not associative. These two expressions are different vectors.
If a · (b × c) = 0, the three vectors are coplanar (volume is zero), NOT that one of the vectors is zero.
The scalar triple product a · (b × c) can be negative, but the volume is the absolute value: V = |a · (b × c)|.
Cyclic permutation preserves the sign: a · (b × c) = b · (c × a). But swapping two vectors flips the sign: a · (c × b) = −a · (b × c).
The vector triple product a × (b × c) lies in the plane of b and c (since it is a linear combination of b and c), but (a × b) × c lies in the plane of a and b.

universalFacts: The scalar triple product a · (b × c) equals the determinant of the 3×3 matrix formed by the components of the three vectors.
The vector triple product BAC-CAB rule is one of the most frequently used identities in vector calculus and physics.
Three vectors are linearly dependent if and only if their scalar triple product is zero — this is the algebraic version of coplanarity.
Jacobi's identity a × (b × c) + b × (c × a) + c × (a × b) = 0 is fundamental in Lie algebra theory.
The scalar triple product is invariant under cyclic permutation of its three vector arguments, which is the algebraic expression of the oriented volume being unchanged.
